newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sees summer gasoline prices remaining low.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sees summer gasoline prices remaining low.

text.p: Gasoline prices should stay relatively low through the summer, then drop slightly for the rest of the year if oil markets remain calm, the U.S. Energy Information Administration said Tuesday.
But prices should rebound by about 5 cents a gallon next spring as the new driving season begins, the Energy Department's statistical and forecasting agency said.
Retail gasoline prices for this year appear to have peaked in January at an average of $1.32 a gallon, and they eased an average of 7 cents a gallon by last month, the administration said.
It projected that prices would stay fairly low through the summer driving season, which ends Labour Day weekend.

The administration also examined the gasoline price spikes in spring 1996 that prompted an outcry by a number of congressmen and complaints that refiners were keeping inventories too tight and making price rises worse.
The administration said the price spikes were "explained largely by markets in crude oil and normal seasonal behaviour."
The winter of 1996-97 was warmer than usual, and new crude supplies arrived from Iraq and other sources, bringing prices down for crude oil and gasoline, it said.

"Retail gasoline prices declined 6 cents per gallon from January through May. As a result of the lower crude oil prices, EIA expects gasoline prices to remain below those of last year during the remainder of the summer driving season," it said.
